label: Extended Foucauldian subjectivation and "care of the self" to religious piety
description: In Politics of Piety (2005), Saba Mahmood mobilized Foucault's late ethics of subjectivation alongside Aristotelian habitus to analyze how disciplined bodily rituals cultivate pious ethical desire rather than mere repression.
dialecticalTension: Decouples Foucauldian subject-formation from strictly secular-transgressive politics.
historicalContext: Ethnography of the Cairo women's mosque movement (2005).

label: Refuted reduction of ethical agency to normative resistance or subversion
description: Engaging Butler's performativity theory, Mahmood argued that equating agency with subverting norms reflects a parochial secular-liberal teleology that obscures how non-liberal traditions form ethical subjects through norm inhabitation.
dialecticalTension: Pits performative subversion against embodied devotional habituation.
